newsitem.title: CAMEROON: Rwanda tribunal official kept waiting in Cameroon.
newsitem.headline: Rwanda tribunal official kept waiting in Cameroon.

text.p: The registrar of the International Criminal Tribunal on Rwanda's 1994 massacres said on Monday he had spent a second day in Cameroon without any progress on the handover of the prime suspect, Colonel Theoneste Bagosora.
Andronico Adede suggested the Cameroon government had not made up its mind on turning over the former army colonel and 11 other genocide suspects whose extradition was decided by Cameroon courts.
He told Reuters he had not been able to meet Justice Minister Laurent Esso since arriving in Yaounde on Monday.

"Another meeting has been set for tomorrow," he said, adding: "The Cameroon government has still not decided. I hope I will finally be received tomorrow and that there will be some progress on the fate of Colonel Bagosora and the others."

Cameroon's courts have ruled that the tribunal, which is investigating the killing by Rwandan Hutu hardliners of up to a million minority Tutsis and moderate Hutus, has the right to extradite Bagosora and the 11 others held in Cameroon.
They ruled that the U.N. court outranked national courts in international law. They declined to rule on a Rwandan extradition request.
Bagosora was a top official at the defence ministry during the masaacres and is one of Rwanda's most wanted men.
Officials say that the handover of the suspects depends on the go-ahead from Cameroon President Paul Biya, which they describe as an administrative formality.
The 12 suspects were arrested in March and April.
